I've been working this land for 30 years in Quzhou. I know the soil, I know the water, and I know what sells. My son works in the city now so it's mostly just me and my wife. Cotton is hard work — picking is brutal — but prices have been decent. Maize I can handle mostly with machines and it doesn't wear me out like cotton does.

I've got 7 mu total. I'll put 4 mu into spring maize and 3 mu into cotton. Maize is simpler, mechanized, and I can manage it without my son around. Cotton needs more attention but 3 mu is manageable for the two of us.

For maize, I'll use hybrid seed — everyone here uses Zhengdan 958 or something similar, I've seen the yields, there's no reason to go back to traditional. I'll rotary till before planting like I always do, do a base fertilizer application then topdress at jointing. Three irrigations from the well — one before planting, one at jointing, one at grain filling. I don't over-irrigate because the electricity costs add up. Two pesticide passes — mostly for corn borer.

For cotton, I'll use an improved Bt variety — bollworm pressure used to be terrible before Bt, I won't go back. Cotton needs more water and more spraying. I'll irrigate four times and spray six times across the season for aphids, mites, and any bollworm escapes. Rotary till in spring before transplanting seedlings.

I'm not pushing inputs to the extreme. I've seen neighbors over-fertilize and it doesn't pay back.
